idScheme: CA-NN (closing audit); chosen so it cannot collide with the project's E-/L-/P-/T-/R-/X-/W- registry

findings.title: TypeScript `Date` is bound as Dart `DateTime`, which fails at runtime in both directions under dart2js
findings.violatedIntent: README 'Correct runtime dispatch'; CLAUDE.md 'Analyzer-clean output is not sufficient evidence for JS dispatch'; design principle 1 (never degrade silently)
findings.evidence: host() maps the checker-confirmed lib `Date` to `DateTime`. package:js does not convert a JS Date to a Dart DateTime (or back). dart2js probe: `external DateTime now()` returning `new Date(...)` throws on `.year`; passing `DateTime.utc(2030)` to `external num yearOf(DateTime d)` delivers a non-Date to JavaScript and throws. dart analyze reports nothing.
findings.reproduction: audit/10-closing-17e8aa9/fixtures/runtime-date/{datelib.d.ts,datelib.js,main.dart}; observed output in fixtures/runtime-date/observed.txt ('now().year threw: JSObject', 'yearOf threw: JSObject')
findings.falsification: Checked whether js_facade_gen's reference cases or the repo's runtime/e2e probes cover Date (they do not), and whether package:js converts DateTime (it does not; dart2js run throws). The finding stands.
findings.consequence: Any binding that returns or accepts a Date compiles and analyzes cleanly but throws when used. Corpus: 13 occurrences in 5 files, including Leaflet `TileEvent.loaded?: Date` (a gated library).
findings.remediation: Lower `Date` to a named, documented interop type (for example a `@JS('Date')` class or a named dynamic typedef) rather than `DateTime`, and add a dart2js runtime probe case for Date in def_files/synthetic/runtime.
findings.rootCause: RC-1 host-type mapping chosen without a runtime probe

findings.title: Watch mode diverges from a cold build when a module file's `declare global` declarations change
findings.location: src/watch.ts:193-243 (dirty propagation: dependents by import, isScript), src/watch.ts:357-369 (seedFiles); commit 17e8aa9 (cf3de40)
findings.violatedIntent: W-01 / CLAUDE.md 'Watch caches must never change output'; watch.ts header 'Its output is identical to a fresh Transpiler.render()'
findings.evidence: Only importers of a changed module file, or every file when a *script* file changes, are regenerated and re-linked. A module file's `declare global { interface X }` is visible to files that never import it, so those files keep stale `resolvedFQN`s and stale render-cache entries.
findings.reproduction: pnpm exec tsx audit/10-closing-17e8aa9/fixtures/watch-global-move.ts (b.dart differs: cold `import 'c.dart' show Gfoo;` vs watch `typedef Gfoo = dynamic;`; single-file add also differs). fixtures/watch-global-augmentation.ts shows link report valid=1 (cold) vs 2 (watch). Logs: logs/watch-global-*.log
findings.falsification: Re-ran the documented differential suite (pnpm test:incremental: 5/5 pass) and two neighbouring scenarios (typeof const and alias change across an import), which do match. Only the non-import global-visibility path diverges.
findings.consequence: During a watch session, consumers of globals declared in module files keep degraded or stale bindings (dynamic instead of the real class, or missing imports) until they are edited or the session restarts; -lv link reports are wrong.
findings.remediation: Treat files containing `declare global` (or any globally visible declaration) like script files for invalidation, or track dependents through resolved checker targets as well as imports. Add the two scenarios to test/watch-differential.test.ts.
findings.rootCause: RC-2 global visibility not modelled across files

findings.title: Barrel re-exports are silently lost or renamed: import-then-export, `export * as ns`, and `export { A as B }`
findings.violatedIntent: README 'Barrels become libraries'; design principle 1 (never degrade silently)
findings.evidence: (a) `import { A } from './a'; export { A };` records a named export with no specifier; linkModuleExports looks for `A` in the barrel file itself, finds nothing, emits no diagnostic, and the barrel library is not emitted. (b) `export * as ns from './a'` is skipped by reExports() and produces no library. (c) `export { A as Renamed } from './a'` emits `export 'a.dart' show A;`, so the public name `Renamed` does not exist in Dart. The CLI prints no emission diagnostic for any of them.
findings.reproduction: audit/10-closing-17e8aa9/fixtures/backend/barrels/*.d.ts; see logs/backend-probes.txt (no reexport-import.dart or nsexport.dart emitted; rename.dart contains `export 'a.dart' show A;`)
findings.falsification: Confirmed that `export * from` and `export { A } from` (same name) work, as the docs claim; only the three listed forms fail.
findings.consequence: Consumers importing a barrel get missing libraries or different names than the TypeScript API, with exit code 0 and no warning.
findings.remediation: Resolve specifier-less named exports through the checker's alias target; emit a typedef or diagnostic for renamed exports (Dart cannot rename on export); emit a MODULE_EXPORT_UNSUPPORTED diagnostic for namespace re-exports.
findings.rootCause: RC-3 module-export linking keyed by file-local terminal names

findings.title: Members named like dart:core `Object` members produce analyzer errors (INVALID_OVERRIDE)
findings.violatedIntent: PLAN.md 'The v1 acceptance test': output passes dart analyze with zero errors
findings.evidence: Member allocation escapes reserved words only; `toString(base: number)`, `hashCode: string`, `runtimeType: number`, `noSuchMethod(x: number)` are emitted verbatim and conflict with Object's signatures.
findings.falsification: A compatible override (`toString(precision?: number)`, as in Leaflet's LatLng) is valid Dart and analyzes cleanly; the defect needs a non-optional parameter or an incompatible property type, which valid TypeScript permits (e.g. bignum `toString(base)`).
findings.consequence: Libraries declaring such members fail the v1 acceptance criterion with hard analyzer errors.
findings.remediation: Treat Object members as reserved in member allocation unless the emitted signature is a valid override: rename to `JS$toString` etc. with `@JS('toString')` through the extension path already used for renamed members.
findings.rootCause: RC-4 member identifier legality ignores Dart class-member constraints

findings.title: A member that shares its enclosing type's name produces analyzer errors
findings.violatedIntent: PLAN.md v1 acceptance test (zero analyzer errors)
findings.evidence: `interface Item { Item: number }` and `class Node2 { Node2(): void }` emit members named like the class; Dart reports MEMBER_WITH_CLASS_NAME, INVALID_FACTORY_NAME_NOT_A_CLASS, CONSTRUCTOR_WITH_RETURN_TYPE, DUPLICATE_CONSTRUCTOR.
findings.falsification: None of the gated corpora contain this shape (they analyze clean); the defect is real for valid TypeScript input.
findings.consequence: Uncompilable library for inputs that use this (rare) pattern.
findings.remediation: Reserve the owner's Dart name during member allocation and route the renamed member through the extension with `@JS('<name>')`.
findings.rootCause: RC-4 member identifier legality ignores Dart class-member constraints

findings.title: Ambient external modules bind `@JS("<module specifier>.<name>")`, a runtime-unresolvable path for most specifiers
findings.violatedIntent: Design principle 1; README 'Correct runtime dispatch'
findings.evidence: `declare module "@scope/pkg" { export class Widget ... }` in a script file emits `@JS("@scope/pkg.Widget")`. dart2js resolves dotted @JS paths from the global object, so `globalThis['@scope/pkg']` is read, which no loader defines. `--js-root` does not apply (fileIsModule is false). No diagnostic. h3 works only because its specifier `h3` equals its browser global.
findings.falsification: Checked h3 (specifier equals the global, e2e passes) and module augmentations (suppressed with a diagnostic). Runtime failure for non-identifier specifiers is by reasoning from dart2js @JS path semantics; not executed.
findings.consequence: Analyzer-clean bindings that throw at first use for ambient modules named like npm packages with scopes, slashes or dashes.
findings.remediation: Emit a diagnostic when a specifier is not a JS identifier path, and allow `--js-root` (or a per-module root option) to supply the global for ambient modules.
findings.rootCause: RC-1 runtime binding decisions without a runtime probe

findings.title: Cross-file global declaration merging is unsupported: partial duplicate classes and `dynamic` use sites
findings.location: src/symbol/fqn.ts:110-117 (FQN includes file), src/symbol/resolve.ts:215-233 (checker candidates -> ambiguous), src/engine/semantic/merge.ts (per-FQN merge); commit 17e8aa9
findings.violatedIntent: CLAUDE.md input contract 'Support ... declaration merging, module/global augmentation'; design principle 1
findings.evidence: Two script files each declaring `interface Settings` (TypeScript merges them globally) produce two partial `Settings` classes in two libraries; `configure(settings: Settings)` becomes `configure(Settings_cdbad5 settings)` with `typedef Settings_cdbad5 = dynamic`. The link is ambiguous; the default CLI prints '0 unresolved references' and exits 0.
findings.falsification: Checked STAGE4_PLAN's merge matrix: it is per-FQN and never states that cross-file global merging is unsupported. Same-file merging works.
findings.consequence: Common DefinitelyTyped patterns (global interfaces augmented in several files, e.g. Window/JQuery plugins) lose typing and members are split across libraries.
findings.remediation: Merge globally visible declarations across files into one canonical symbol (or document the limitation and emit a diagnostic at default verbosity).
findings.rootCause: RC-2 global visibility not modelled across files

findings.title: Default CLI output omits link failures (missing/ambiguous type references)
findings.violatedIntent: Design principle 1 (never degrade silently); R-02 intent (CLI always prints the unresolved count)
findings.evidence: processFiles prints semantic warnings, emission diagnostics and *module* resolution counts. LinkReport.broken is printed only with -l. A run with a broken link prints 'Module resolution: 0 unresolved references' and exits 0.
findings.falsification: Degradations are still named and documented inside the generated file, so the output itself is not silent; only the console summary is.
findings.consequence: Users and CI scripts see a clean run while some types degraded to dynamic.
findings.remediation: Always print the broken-symbol count (and ambiguous edge count) with a pointer to -lv.
findings.rootCause: RC-5 console summary covers module resolution only

findings.title: A bigint literal type with numeric separators (`1_000n`) aborts the whole run
findings.violatedIntent: Input contract (valid declaration syntax); proportionate failure
findings.evidence: BigInt('1_000') throws SyntaxError; the statement fails with STATEMENT_DECLARATION_ERROR and transpile() blocks every write (GENERATION_FAILED). Number('1_000') returns NaN silently for the number case.
findings.reproduction: audit/10-closing-17e8aa9/fixtures/backend/bigintsep/bigintsep.d.ts -> 'Cannot convert 1_000 to a BigInt', exit 1, no files
findings.falsification: Not present in the 1,661-file corpus (stress passes), so prevalence is low.
findings.consequence: One valid literal prevents output for the whole program.
findings.remediation: Strip `_` separators before BigInt()/Number(), or use the checker's literal value.
findings.rootCause: RC-6 literal values parsed from raw source text (see open T-11)

findings.title: The CLI/programmatic path does not report TypeScript syntax errors; malformed input yields plausible output and exit 0
findings.violatedIntent: transpileFromString comment 'Surface syntax errors rather than silently producing empty output'; design principle 1
findings.evidence: Only transpileFromString collects pre-emit diagnostics. `interface Broken { a: string` (missing brace) via the CLI writes broken.dart and exits 0 with no warning.
findings.falsification: The TypeScript parser's recovery happened to keep the member here; other malformed inputs can lose declarations without notice.
findings.consequence: Typos in hand-written declaration files go unnoticed.
findings.remediation: Report syntactic diagnostics of input files in AnalysisReport and print them in the CLI.

findings.title: File names containing `'` or `$` produce invalid Dart import/export directives
findings.violatedIntent: E-32 intent (central Dart-string escaping for every emitted string)
findings.evidence: URIs are interpolated raw into single-quoted Dart strings. `my lib.d.ts` importing `./it's` and `./cost$x` yields UNTERMINATED_STRING_LITERAL, URI_WITH_INTERPOLATION and cascade errors.
findings.falsification: A space in a file name analyzes cleanly; only quote and `$` fail.
findings.consequence: Uncompilable output for unusual but legal file names.
findings.remediation: Escape or percent-encode URIs (dartString or Uri-encode path segments) for import/export directives.
findings.rootCause: RC-7 emitted strings outside the central escaper

findings.title: Private-use characters in source text are interpreted as backend placeholder tokens
findings.violatedIntent: Generated output faithfully reflects input; trust boundary between input text and emitter control tokens
findings.evidence: Import/support/exports placeholders are U+E000-E004 and U+E010-E011 and are replaced with regexes over the whole library text, including docs and names copied from input. A doc comment containing `\uE0000\uE001Foo\uE002` is rewritten to `Foo`.
findings.falsification: Input needs deliberate private-use characters; in a library with imports the same sequence can add a name to an import's `show` list.
findings.consequence: Crafted or corrupted input can alter generated code or documentation; integrity issue, not code execution.
findings.remediation: Escape or strip these code points from copied text before emission, or use placeholder tokens that cannot occur in input.
findings.rootCause: RC-7 emitted strings outside the central escaper

findings.title: Link report memoisation misreports symbols inside a reference cycle
findings.violatedIntent: LinkReport as the honest link measure (S2, L-08)
findings.evidence: When checkDeps re-enters an in-progress node it returns LinkedResolved, and the caller caches that provisional answer. With A -> B, B -> A, A -> Missing, B is reported LinkedResolved although it depends on broken A (order-dependent).
findings.falsification: Emission does not read LinkResult, so generated Dart is unaffected.
findings.consequence: -lv reports and the dependency graph (red nodes) under-count broken symbols.
findings.remediation: Compute states over strongly connected components, or do not cache provisional results produced while a cycle member is in progress.

findings.title: `.d.mts` / `.d.cts` inputs are silently dropped
findings.violatedIntent: Input contract: declaration files
findings.evidence: Explicit `-d mod.d.mts` alone exits 1 with 'No .d.ts files found'. Mixed with .d.ts inputs, .d.mts/.d.cts files are filtered without a message.
findings.falsification: Files reached through imports are still resolved by TypeScript; only explicit inputs are filtered.
findings.consequence: Packages that ship only .d.mts/.d.cts entry points cannot be bound directly.
findings.remediation: Accept .d.mts/.d.cts (mapping output to .dart) or warn when explicit inputs are skipped.

findings.title: Watch mode computes its root directory by string prefix, not by path segment
findings.violatedIntent: Watch mode rebuilds whenever an input changes
findings.evidence: reduce() keeps `common` while `directory.startsWith(common)`. For inputs in /p/types and /p/types2 the root stays /p/types, so changes under /p/types2 are never observed.
findings.reproduction: Reasoning from the code path; not executed (requires an interactive watcher).
findings.falsification: Inputs under one directory, or directories without a shared string prefix, are unaffected.
findings.consequence: Some inputs are silently not watched.
findings.remediation: Reuse resolvedInputRoot() (segment-wise) from transpiler.ts.

findings.title: A class whose constructors are all private/protected gets Dart's implicit public constructor
findings.violatedIntent: E-35 intent (no implicit construction of non-constructable runtime types)
findings.evidence: inheritedConstructors() filters private constructors; because declaration.constructors is non-empty, no external constructor is written either, so Dart supplies an implicit `Singleton()`.
findings.falsification: Analyzer is clean; dart2js behaviour of calling the implicit constructor on an @JS class was not executed.
findings.consequence: Dart code can call a constructor TypeScript forbids.
findings.remediation: Emit an unreachable private Dart constructor (`external Name._();`) or make the class abstract when no public constructor exists.

findings.title: CI installs Dart `stable` while the analyzer baseline is an exact census for Dart 3.13
findings.violatedIntent: Reproducible acceptance gate (X-09, S6.2)
findings.evidence: baseline.json says 'Dart SDK 3.13'; the gate fails on any changed count or category. setup-dart `sdk: stable` follows new releases.
findings.reproduction: Reasoning; the gate passed with 3.13.7 in this audit.
findings.falsification: Today stable is 3.13.7 and the gate passes.
findings.consequence: A new Dart release (new deprecations or lints) turns CI red without a code change, or changes what the gate certifies.
findings.remediation: Pin the SDK in CI to the baseline's version and bump both together.

findings.title: CI hardening: actions pinned to mutable tags and no explicit `permissions:`
findings.location: .github/workflows/ci.yml (actions/checkout@v4, pnpm/action-setup@v4, actions/setup-node@v4, dart-lang/setup-dart@v1; no permissions block)
findings.violatedIntent: Supply-chain best practice
findings.evidence: Static read of the workflow.
findings.falsification: The workflow publishes nothing and has no secrets, which limits impact; the token's default scope depends on repository settings (not verifiable from the tree).
findings.consequence: A compromised action tag would run with the job's token.
findings.remediation: Pin actions by commit SHA and set `permissions: contents: read`.

findings.title: Lockfile pins dev tooling with critical advisories (Vitest UI arbitrary file read/execute, tinypool RCE gadgets)
findings.location: pnpm-lock.yaml (vitest 3.2.4, tinypool); package.json devDependencies; CLAUDE.md documents `pnpm test:ui`
findings.violatedIntent: Dependency risk management
findings.evidence: pnpm audit: 53 advisories in the full tree (3 critical, 26 high). Critical: vitest <3.2.6 GHSA-5xrq-8626-4rwp (Vitest UI server, which `pnpm test:ui` starts), tinypool GHSA-5gmw-xhrv-c9v3 / GHSA-85c8-ppgw-ccpr.
findings.falsification: None ship in the npm package (dev-only); exposure needs the UI server listening or attacker-controlled worker options.
findings.consequence: Contributors running the documented UI command expose local files to a malicious web page or network peer while it runs.
findings.remediation: Upgrade vitest/@vitest/* to >=3.2.6 (and tinypool) and re-run the gates.

findings.title: Production transitive glob libraries carry high ReDoS advisories
findings.location: pnpm-lock.yaml: ts-morph > @ts-morph/common > minimatch/@isaacs/brace-expansion, tinyglobby > picomatch; fast-glob > micromatch > picomatch
findings.violatedIntent: Dependency risk management
findings.evidence: pnpm audit --prod: 9 advisories (6 high, 3 moderate), all ReDoS/DoS or matching errors in glob matching (logs/pnpm-audit-prod.txt).
findings.falsification: Glob patterns come from the user running the CLI, so the DoS is self-inflicted; the published package ships no lockfile, so npm installs resolve patched versions where ranges allow.
findings.consequence: Low for end users; the repository's own CI and dev environment run the pinned vulnerable versions.
findings.remediation: Refresh the lockfile (`pnpm update`) and re-run the gates.

findings.title: Documented gate numbers drifted from measured values
findings.location: CLAUDE.md (gates paragraph, corpus table), README.md ('1,655-file stress corpus'), PLAN.md S6 row ('bundle 252 KB'), audit/FINDINGS.md post-S5/S6 baseline, test/stress.test.ts:6 ('1,654-file')
findings.violatedIntent: CLAUDE.md maintenance contract (re-measure baselines)
findings.evidence: Measured at 17e8aa9: def_files has 1,661 tracked .d.ts (1,654 + runtime probe + 6 watch fixtures), stress reports 720/1661 empty (docs: 1,655 and 719); test:s4 54/54 (docs: 53/53); bundle chunk 262.7 KB + cli 15.3 KB + watch 16.1 KB (docs: 252 KB); coverage 90.43% lines (docs: 90.1%).
findings.falsification: All gates pass; only the recorded numbers are stale.
findings.consequence: Readers cannot tell a regression from drift; the 'exact' numbers in CLAUDE.md are not exact.
findings.remediation: Re-measure and update the numbers in one commit; consider generating them from gate output.

findings.title: Finding registry integrity: `X-16` is assigned to two different findings; `Where` columns point to deleted files
findings.location: audit/FINDINGS.md:107 and :183 (two X-16 rows); rows such as E-14, E-19, E-31 citing `emitter/old/*`
findings.violatedIntent: CLAUDE.md 'never renumber or delete an ID'; stable IDs referenced by commits
findings.evidence: X-16 is the coverage-provider finding (4.16) and also the `.gitignore` Dart-fixture finding. Several FIXED rows still cite `src/engine/emitter/old/...` paths that S5 deleted.
findings.falsification: Not applicable (documentation fact).
findings.consequence: Commit messages and CHANGELOG references to X-16 are ambiguous.
findings.remediation: Give the .gitignore finding a new ID (keep X-16 for coverage) and refresh stale locations.

findings.title: Several registered fixes work but have no regression test
findings.location: test/** (no case for P-18, E-44's NATIVE_NAME_CONFLICT diagnostic, or a TypeScript `abstract class` for E-20)
findings.violatedIntent: Closing-audit requirement: registered fixes are real, tested and complete
findings.evidence: Runtime check at 17e8aa9: P-18 drops `this:` from function types, E-20 emits `abstract class Shape`, and E-44 reports NATIVE_NAME_CONFLICT. A search of test/ finds no assertion covering these paths.
findings.falsification: Snapshots might cover them indirectly: the P-18 and E-44 shapes do not occur in the snapshot inputs; the E-20 TS abstract class does not either.
findings.consequence: Regressions in these paths would pass the suite.
findings.remediation: Add focused cases to test/decl/decl-emitter.test.ts.

findings.title: No upgrade or rollback notes for existing 0.5.0 users
findings.violatedIntent: Release readiness (S6.10); 'drop-in replacement' positioning
findings.evidence: 1.0.0 changes the generated API relative to 0.5.0 (for example h3 `Anon_h3_CoordIJ` -> `CoordIJ`, fields -> getter/setter pairs, overload names `f_1`/`f_2`, constructors), but CHANGELOG has no breaking-changes or migration section, and no rollback (dist-tag) note exists.
findings.falsification: CLI flags are backward compatible with 0.5.0 (all old flags still exist).
findings.consequence: Users regenerating with 1.0.0 meet unannounced source-level breaks in their Dart code.
findings.remediation: Add a 'Breaking changes since 0.5.0' section and a release/rollback checklist (npm dist-tag `next`, deprecate).
